caption:
On $60,000 of sole trader profit in 2026–27, income tax and Medicare come to roughly $8,600 after offsets: about 14%.

So why do accountants say put 25% aside? Because profit grows, the ATO starts collecting instalments in advance after your first year, and if you're registered for GST, that money was never yours to begin with.

Put the buffer away. Future you says thanks.

Assumes resident, no other income, no HELP debt, turnover under $5M. General info only, not personal advice.
